memory_candidates.content: When consolidating N hand-copied literal allowlists (or similar fixed-constant lists) scattered across sibling scripts into one shared definition, model the new library on an existing proven sourced-library shape (e.g. derived-artifact-probe-lib.sh): a header stating contract + fail-open posture + explicit consumer enumeration; sourced, never executed; sets no shell options a caller inherits. If the list is a fixed constant of the system itself (not derived from external config like .claude-extensions.json), build the function's output with `printf` from a literal, not `jq` -- this avoids an unnecessary jq dependency for a value that never actually needs JSON querying to produce. Each consumer should implement its OWN fallback to the pre-migration literal value on a source/resolution failure (never let the shared library itself encode the fallback, since a failed source means code inside it cannot run), so a library failure is behavior-preserving (reproduces pre-shared-library behavior exactly) rather than silently narrowing scope.

To confirm a new negative/non-regression test assertion (e.g. 'path X is still dropped as out-of-scope') is a genuine guard and not a tautology, temporarily mutate the probed value so the assertion's premise should flip (e.g. widen an allowlist library to include the specific out-of-scope path under test, or to a blanket prefix that covers it), re-run the suite and confirm the target assertion goes red, then restore the original file and verify byte-identical via `diff` before re-running to confirm green again. Pick the widening target carefully: a prefix like ["specs/"] only probes paths actually under specs/ -- if the genuine-excursion fixture path lives outside specs/ (e.g. other/outside.txt), that widening will not flip it and the sanity check will falsely appear to pass; widen to literally include the exact excursion path instead when the fixture lives in a different namespace.

deploy-headless.sh auto-runs the deployed generate-context-line-counts.sh --write before every deploy, but does NOT auto-run sync-manifest-scripts.sh. When a source-store task adds new files under agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/ or scripts/tests/, run `bash agent-system/extensions/<ext>/scripts/sync-manifest-scripts.sh --write` manually (registers missing provides.scripts entries) before redeploying, or the new files may not be correctly tracked/verified even though the deploy mechanism itself (manager.resync_all, a Lua plugin) may still copy them. Also note: generate-context-line-counts.sh refuses to run from the source-store scripts/ path directly (its own ../.. root resolution assumes a deployed tree) -- always invoke the DEPLOYED copy (.claude/scripts/generate-context-line-counts.sh --write), which still writes back to the SOURCE index-entries.json files by design.
